cases.purpose: A lone ESC followed by a pause longer than the grace returns 'esc 27' and does not absorb the next key; an incomplete CSI prefix (ESC [ with nothing after it) also returns 'esc 27' at the grace boundary, its '[' is consumed, and the following key decodes on its own.
cases.script: bashtermraw raw; kgetch read > esc; kgetch read > k1; kgetch read > partial; kgetch read > k2; bashtermraw cooked
cases.oracle: kgetch help text (kgetch.c kgetch_doc): ESC grace is 50 ms; ESC-prefixed matching has total cap max(400 ms, ESCDELAY*8); BASHESCDELAY or BASHKGETCH_ESCDELAY sets ESCDELAY; BASHKGETCH_TERMINFO names a key_*=sequence fixture layered over the ANSI table; read prints 'NAME CODE' (esc 27, char N, none 0 at EOF). The handling of an incomplete prefix (return esc 27 at the first 50 ms gap, prefix bytes dropped) is implementation-defined in kgetch.c bk_read_key, not stated in the help text.
cases.comparison: contract: decoded key names written by kgetch read on the private PTY; no external reference

cases.purpose: Prefix bytes that keep arriving every 20 ms (inside the 50 ms slice) cannot extend one read beyond the default 400 ms cap: the first read returns 'esc 27' after 380-750 ms; the remaining dripped bytes and the final 'Z' are decoded by later reads (not lost or merged), and EOF gives 'none 0'.
cases.script:
unset BASHESCDELAY BASHKGETCH_ESCDELAY
export BASHKGETCH_TERMINFO=$PWD/long.ti
/usr/bin/python3 drip.py 0.02 40 | {
  cd run || exit 1
  t0=$EPOCHREALTIME; kgetch read > first; t1=$EPOCHREALTIME
  : > rest; i=0
  while (( i < 100 )); do
    kgetch read > one; IFS= read -r line < one
    printf '%s\n' "$line" >> rest
    [[ $line == 'none 0' ]] && break
    i=$((i+1))
  done
  ms=$(( (${t1/./} - ${t0/./}) / 1000 ))
  if (( ms >= 380 && ms <= 750 )); then echo window-ok; else echo "window-bad $ms"; fi > elapsed
  ones=0 other=''
  while IFS= read -r line; do
    if [[ $line == 'char 49' && -z $other ]]; then ones=$((ones+1)); else other+="$line;"; fi
  done < rest
  if (( ones >= 5 && ones + 2 <= 40 )); then echo ones-after-cap-ok; else echo "ones-bad $ones"; fi > remainder
  printf '%s\n' "$other" > tail
}

cases.comparison: contract, semantic timing predicate: exact first-read token; elapsed window 380-750 ms around the 400 ms cap (scheduler tolerance); later reads give at least 5 'char 49' then exactly 'char 90' and 'none 0'. The split point between capped and later bytes depends on timing and is not compared.

files.drip.py:
import os, sys, time
gap, n = float(sys.argv[1]), int(sys.argv[2])
os.write(1, b"\x1b[")
for _ in range(n):
    time.sleep(gap)
    os.write(1, b"1")
time.sleep(0.3)
os.write(1, b"Z")

# private fixture: a 63-byte sequence so a slow prefix cannot complete before the cap
key_f5=\E[111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111~
